culture-cycles.note: Holidays treated like Sundays under the cantonal rest-day laws (SECO table). The 1 August national day is the only federal holiday. Holidays on a Sunday are not moved.

layers.process: The Swiss National Park is closed in winter, as a wildlife rest zone, and entry is forbidden then. Trails are generally open from mid-May to mid-November, and each trail's open or closed status depends on weather and altitude (the park publishes it). Visits are allowed in daytime only, from the start of morning civil twilight to the end of evening civil twilight; the same limit applies to overnight stays in vehicles along the Ofenpass road.

laws.rule: In the Swiss National Park, leaving the marked paths and post-marked rest areas is strictly forbidden. Dogs are not allowed, even on a lead. Campfires, swimming in lakes and streams, cycling of any kind, and flying of any kind (including drones) are not permitted. Picking or removing anything natural (animals, plants, sticks, stones) and littering are not allowed. Park wardens can issue fixed on-the-spot fines under the Graubünden fine ordinance (OBVN, 498.210); the amounts sit in an annex that could not be read here.
laws.heading: Schutzbestimmungen, Schweizerischer Nationalpark; Nationalparkordnung (BR 498.200)

laws.rule: In Graubünden each commune may charge a guest tax (Gästetaxe) on overnight guests, and the proceeds must go to tourist facilities and events, not ordinary council costs (art. 22 of the commune and church tax law). The amount is set by each commune, so check the local regulation.
laws.heading: Gesetz über die Gemeinde- und Kirchensteuern (BR 720.200), art. 22

laws.rule: Smoking is banned indoors and outdoors on school grounds, school sports facilities, and child and youth meeting and care places (art. 9(1)). Smoking-only venues (Raucherbetriebe) are not allowed in the canton (art. 9(3)). The health law has fines of up to CHF 20,000 (about A$34,548) for breaches of art. 9. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CHF 0.5789.
laws.heading: Gesetz zum Schutz der Gesundheit im Kanton Graubünden (BR 500.000), art. 9

laws.rule: When forest and field fire danger is raised, lighting fires outside built-up areas is banned in Graubünden. The canton announces the danger publicly. Communes may allow exceptions for safe fireplaces outside the forest.
laws.heading: Kantonales Waldgesetz (BR 920.100), art. 31b
